mainTopic: When must we worry that a widow still needs ייבום, and what does the case of 'this is my brother' teach about answering 'I do not know'?
overview: The amud opens with two stories about dying men whose words might free their wives from ייבום. In the first, a dying man says his wife is 'fit for a כהן גדול.' רבא wants to believe him, based on רבי יוחנן's rule that a husband who says 'I divorced my wife' is believed. אביי points to a second version of רבי יוחנן that says the opposite, and argues that a reconciling answer is not enough to rely on in practice, so רבא tells רב נתן בר אמי to be concerned. In the second story, a man with a חזקה of having no brothers also says so himself before he dies. רב יוסף sees nothing to worry about, but אביי raises a rumor of witnesses overseas, and רבא again rules to be concerned. The גמרא then returns to the משנה of 'this is my brother' and concludes that the other brothers are saying 'we do not know.' From this רבא learns that someone who answers a money claim with 'I do not know' is פטור. אביי begins to respond, and his words continue on the next amud.

steps.title: A dying man says his wife is fit for a כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: A dying man is asked whom his wife may marry after his death. He answers that she is 'fit for a כהן גדול.'
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man who was dying. People asked him: 'Your wife, whom can she marry?' He said: 'She is fit even for a כהן גדול.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life story that sets up the question. Can we trust a dying man who says his wife will not need ייבום?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a man dies without children and has a brother, his widow needs ייבום or חליצה. By saying she is fit for a כהן גדול, the man claims she is completely free and needs no ייבום. The question is whether his word is enough.

phrases.english: There was a certain man who was dying,
they said to him: His wife — to whom may she marry?
phrases.notes: They are really asking whether she will need ייבום after he dies.

phrases.english: He said to them: She is fit for a High Priest.
phrases.notes: This is a way of saying she is totally free, with no ייבום holding her back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the first story of this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: a dying husband claims his wife needs no ייבום.

steps.title: רבא: the husband is believed, like one who says he divorced
steps.stepSummary: רבא says there is nothing to worry about. He cites רבי יוחנן, who rules that a husband who says 'I divorced my wife' is believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What should we worry about? רב חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן that a husband who says 'I divorced my wife' is believed!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rules that the woman is free. He brings a statement of רבי יוחנן as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא compares this man to a husband who reports a divorce. If the husband is believed about a divorce, he can also be believed that his wife is free of ייבום.

keyTerms.meaning: what should we be worried about for her?

phrases.english: Rava said: What should we be worried about for her?

phrases.aramaic: הָא אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
phrases.english: Didn't Rav Chiyya bar Abba say
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
A husband who said 'I divorced my wife' is believed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a ruling on the story from step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That the dying man is believed and his wife needs no ייבום.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן, as quoted by רב חייא בר אבא: a husband who says he divorced his wife is believed.

steps.title: אביי: another version says the husband is not believed
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes רבי יצחק בר יוסף. In his version, רבי יוחנן said the husband is NOT believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But when רבי יצחק בר יוסף came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן that a husband who says 'I divorced my wife' is NOT believed!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבא's proof. There is a second report of רבי יוחנן's words that says the exact opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's whole proof rested on רבי יוחנן believing the husband. If another reliable report says רבי יוחנן did not believe him, the proof falls apart.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא כִּי אֲתָא רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף
phrases.english: But when Rabbi Yitzchak bar Yosef came,
he said that Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: בַּעַל שֶׁאָמַר ״גֵּרַשְׁתִּי אֶת אִשְׁתִּי״ – אֵינוֹ נֶאֱמָן!
phrases.english: A husband who said 'I divorced my wife' is not believed!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא כִּי אֲתָא רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source רבא used in step 2.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A second report of רבי יוחנן says the opposite, so the source cannot support רבא's ruling.

steps.title: רבא: the two reports were already reconciled
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that we already explained the two reports. One is about the past and one is about the future.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Didn't we already explain them? One statement is about the past, and the other is about the future.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his proof. He reminds אביי that the two versions of רבי יוחנן do not really argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband is not believed to make the divorce count backwards in time. He is believed about her status from now on. Our case is about her status going forward, so both versions agree he is believed.

keyTerms.meaning: backwards in time, about the past

phrases.english: He said to him: Didn't we already reconcile them —
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. The meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: here it is about the past, and here it is about the future?

steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the two sources into different situations (past vs. future).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two reports of רבי יוחנן contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Not believed about the past, believed about the future. Our case is about the future, so he is believed.

steps.title: אביי: we cannot rely on a reconciling answer
steps.stepSummary: אביי replies that an answer made up to settle a contradiction is not strong enough to rely on in practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should we really get up and rely on answers?!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rejects רבא's answer as a basis for a real ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי does not say the answer is wrong. He says it may not be what רבי יוחנן truly meant. With a woman's status at stake, we must still worry about the version that says the husband is not believed.

phrases.english: And should we get up and rely on answers?!
phrases.notes: This is still אביי talking. A clever answer is fine for learning, but too shaky for a practical ruling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on רבא's answer in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the answer for a practical ruling. It does not prove the answer false.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The answer may not be correct, so the stricter version still has to be taken into account.

steps.title: רבא tells רב נתן בר אמי to be concerned
steps.stepSummary: In the end, רבא himself instructs רב נתן בר אמי to be concerned about this case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נתן בר אמי: Be concerned about it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא accepts אביי's point. He rules strictly in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא had first wanted to free the woman, but now he says we must worry that she still needs ייבום. אביי's warning about relying on reconciling answers wins out in practice.
steps.whatToRemember: A dying man who says his wife is free is backed by one version of רבי יוחנן. Since another version disagrees, and we do not rely on reconciling answers in practice, רבא rules that we must be concerned.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a general principle: an answer that settles a contradiction is good for learning, but it is not enough to permit something in practice.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב נָתָן בַּר אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Natan bar Ami:
Be concerned about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב נָתָן בַּר אַמֵּי: חוּשׁ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא's practical ruling after אביי's objection in step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: We must be concerned that the woman still needs ייבום, despite the husband's statement.

steps.title: A man presumed to have no brothers says so before dying
steps.stepSummary: A second story: a man is known to have no brothers, and before he dies he himself says he has no brothers.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man whom we presumed to have no brothers. At the time of his death, he said he had no brothers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new story. This sets up the next question about whether his widow needs ייבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here there are two things in the woman's favor: the community's חזקה that he has no brothers, and his own statement. If he truly has no brothers, there is no one to do ייבום.

phrases.english: There was a certain man who was presumed by us
to have no brothers,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲמַר בִּשְׁעַת מִיתָה דְּלֵית לֵיהּ אַחֵי.
phrases.english: and he said at the time of death that he has no brothers.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא דַּהֲוָה מוּחְזָק לַן דְּלֵית לֵיהּ אַחֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new, related story about a dying man's words and ייבום.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: both a חזקה and the man's own words say he has no brothers.

steps.title: רב יוסף: there are two reasons not to worry
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says there is nothing to worry about. The man has a חזקה of having no brothers, and he also said so himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: What should we worry about? First, we know him as having no brothers. And also, he said at the time of death that he has none.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף rules that the widow is free of ייבום. He gives two reasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the first story, here the man's words are backed up by a חזקה. Two supports together seem strong enough to free her.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מַאי לֵיחוּשׁ לַהּ?
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: What should we be worried about for her?

phrases.aramaic: חֲדָא, דְּמוּחְזָק לַן דְּלֵית לֵיהּ אַחִין.
phrases.english: One, he is presumed by us to have no brothers.

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד, הָא אָמַר בִּשְׁעַת מִיתָה דְּלֵית לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: And furthermore, he said at the time of death that he has none.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: מַאי לֵיחוּשׁ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a ruling on the story in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The widow does not need ייבום, because of the חזקה and the man's own statement.

steps.title: אביי: there is a rumor of witnesses overseas
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף. People are saying that witnesses overseas know the man has brothers.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But people say there are witnesses overseas who know that he has brothers!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב יוסף's ruling. A rumor points the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even with a חזקה and the man's own words, a public rumor of witnesses who know otherwise may be reason enough to worry. אביי says we cannot simply ignore that report.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:

phrases.aramaic: הָא אָמְרִי דְּאִיכָּא עֵדִים בִּמְדִינַת הַיָּם
phrases.english: But people say that there are witnesses overseas
who know that he has brothers!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא אָמְרִי דְּאִיכָּא עֵדִים בִּמְדִינַת הַיָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's ruling in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that there is nothing to worry about.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rumor of witnesses who know he has brothers gives a real reason to worry, despite the חזקה and his own words.

steps.title: רב יוסף: Far-away witnesses do not count
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף defends his ruling. Witnesses who are not here cannot undo the man's חזקה, just as רבי חנינא ruled for a captive woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, in any event, those witnesses are not here in front of us. Isn't this just like רבי חנינא's ruling? רבי חנינא said: the witnesses are off in some far place, and because of that she should be forbidden?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers אביי's challenge. A rumor about witnesses somewhere far away is not enough to worry about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף says we only go by what is in front of us. The man has a חזקה of no brothers, and witnesses who are not here cannot break it. He backs this up with רבי חנינא, who did not forbid a captive woman just because people said there were witnesses somewhere else.

keyTerms.meaning: They are not here before us
Witnesses far away, literally 'in the north'

phrases.english: Now, in any event,
phrases.notes: This is רב יוסף answering אביי's challenge from the last step.

phrases.english: they are not here before us;
isn't this the same as רבי חנינא's case?
For רבי חנינא said:
the witnesses are off in the north,
phrases.notes: 'The north' just means some faraway place. רבי חנינא said this about a woman who had been taken captive.

phrases.english: and because of that she should be forbidden?!

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits which evidence matters: only witnesses who are actually present can break a חזקה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A rumor about witnesses overseas should make us worry that the man has brothers.
steps.terutzMaskana: Witnesses who are not here do not break the חזקה, just as in רבי חנינא's case.

steps.title: אביי: A captive is not the same as a married woman
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the comparison. We are lenient with a captive for a special reason, and we should not carry that leniency over to a married woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: If we were lenient with a captive woman, it is because she makes herself repulsive to her captor. Should we then be lenient with a married woman?!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף's proof from רבי חנינא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The captive had an extra reason to be trusted: she makes herself unattractive so the captor leaves her alone. Here there is no such reason, and the question involves a married woman, which is far more serious. So רבי חנינא's leniency does not carry over.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who was taken captive

phrases.english: אביי said to him:
If we were lenient with a captive woman,
it is because she makes herself repulsive
to her captor;
should we be lenient with a married woman?!
phrases.notes: If the man really has brothers, his widow is still tied to them and cannot marry someone else, so this is a serious matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from רבי חנינא brought in step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the comparison to the captive woman, not רבי חנינא's ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The captive case had a special reason to be lenient, and a married woman is a more serious case.

steps.title: רבא rules to be concerned
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells רב נתן בר אמי to take the rumor of witnesses seriously.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נתן בר אמי: Be concerned about it.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the practical ruling for the case: we do worry about the rumor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא sides with אביי's caution. Even though the man had a חזקה and said so himself, the rumor of witnesses is enough to hold back until the matter is clear.
steps.whatToRemember: When a married woman is involved, even a rumor of far-away witnesses is enough reason to be concerned, despite a חזקה.

phrases.english: רבא said
to רב נתן בר אמי:
Be concerned about it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה רבא לרב נתן בר אמי חוש לה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling after the back-and-forth between אביי and רב יוסף.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: We worry about the rumored witnesses and do not let the woman remarry yet.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: 'This is my brother'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה: a man who says 'this is my brother' is not believed.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'This is my brother' — he is not believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. This sets up the questions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man is not believed to make someone an heir alongside his other brothers. As the משנה goes on to say, the new 'brother' only shares in the portion of the one who spoke up.

keyTerms.meaning: The base text the גמרא discusses

phrases.english: 'This is my brother' —
phrases.notes: This is a quote from our משנה, about a man speaking of someone the family does not know as a brother.

phrases.english: he is not believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story and returns to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man who says 'this is my brother' is not believed against the other brothers.

steps.title: What do the other brothers say?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the other brothers claim. If they agree he is their brother, why does he only take from one brother's share?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what are the other brothers saying? If they say 'he is our brother,' why does he take only from this one's portion and nothing more?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wants to know the exact situation in the משנה. It rules out the possibility that the other brothers agree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If all the brothers admitted he was a brother, he would get a full share from everyone. Since the משנה limits him to the speaker's portion, the others must not be agreeing.

phrases.english: And what are the others saying?
If they say 'he is our brother,'
why should he take with him only from his portion
and nothing more?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the case the משנה just described.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the other brothers claim about the man.

steps.title: They must be saying he is not their brother
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the other brothers deny he is their brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they must be saying: 'He is not our brother.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers an answer: the other brothers deny him. It is stated with a question mark because the next step will test it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains why he only shares in the speaker's portion. Only the speaker admits the relationship, so only the speaker loses money.

phrases.english: Rather, they are saying
'he is not our brother'?

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא דקא אמרי לאו אחינו הוא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the remaining possibility after step 14 ruled out the brothers agreeing.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The other brothers deny that he is their brother.

steps.title: Challenge from the end of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The end of the משנה says the brothers inherit property that came to him from elsewhere. How can they, if they said he is not their brother?
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the last part of the משנה: if property came to him from somewhere else, his brothers inherit together with him. But they said 'he is not our brother'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 15 using the end of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the other brothers deny he is a brother, they should not be able to inherit from him. Yet the משנה lets them share in his outside property. So the reading 'they deny him' does not fit.
steps.confusionAlert: 'His brothers' here means the speaker's brothers, the ones who supposedly denied the man.

phrases.english: Say the last clause:
if property came to him
from somewhere else,
his brothers inherit together with him.
phrases.notes: The משנה is talking about after the man in question dies.

phrases.english: But they said about him:
'he is not our brother'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the other brothers say 'he is not our brother.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The end of the משנה lets them inherit from him, which contradicts their denial.

steps.title: The brothers say 'we do not know'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the other brothers neither agree nor deny. They say they do not know whether he is their brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the case is needed where the other brothers say: 'We do not know' whether he is our brother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the קשיא from step 16 by changing what the other brothers are claiming. They are not saying 'he is not our brother.' They are saying 'we don't know.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the brothers don't know, he cannot force them to give him a share, since he has no proof. But they never denied him, so nothing stops them from inheriting what came to him from elsewhere, based on the brother who said he is their brother. Both halves of the משנה now fit.

keyTerms.meaning: No, it is needed only for (this case). It narrows the case to a specific situation.

steps.confusionAlert: 'We do not know' is not the same as 'he is not our brother.' The whole answer depends on the brothers staying in the middle, neither agreeing nor denying.

phrases.english: No, it is necessary only
where they say: 'We do not know.'
phrases.notes: 'They' are the other brothers. They don't know whether he is their brother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 16 by changing the brothers' claim from denial to 'we do not know.'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The other brothers deny that he is their brother, so they should not be able to inherit from him.
steps.terutzMaskana: The brothers say 'we do not know.' He cannot take a share from them without proof, but they can inherit from him.

steps.title: רבא: someone who answers 'I do not know' is exempt
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns from this case that if someone claims 'you have my מנה' and the other answers 'I do not know,' that person is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This teaches that if one person says, 'You have a מנה of mine,' and the other says, 'I do not know,' he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא takes the brothers' case and turns it into a general rule about money claims.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The brothers who say 'we do not know' don't have to give the claimed brother a share. So, says רבא, anyone who answers a money claim with 'I do not know' also does not have to pay. A 'certain' claim does not beat an 'I'm not sure' answer when the money is in the other person's hands.

keyTerms.meaning: This is to say. It introduces a rule learned from a source.
You have a מנה (100 זוז) of mine
Exempt, does not have to pay

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the famous question of בָּרִי וְשֶׁמָּא (a sure claim against an unsure answer), which comes up across ש״ס in money cases.

phrases.english: Rava said: That is to say:
'I have a maneh in your possession,'
and the other says, 'I do not know' –
he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general rule about money claims from the case set up in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who answers a sure money claim with 'I do not know' is exempt (בָּרִי וְשֶׁמָּא – שֶׁמָּא wins).

steps.title: אביי begins to respond to רבא
steps.stepSummary: אביי starts to speak in reaction to רבא's rule. His actual words continue on the next amud.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. אביי is about to respond to רבא's rule, and his words come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the opening 'אביי said' appears here. In context, אביי is about to question whether רבא's rule can really be learned from the brothers' case. Wait for his full words before deciding what he holds.

phrases.english: Abaye said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces אביי's reaction to רבא's rule in step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Expected to challenge whether רבא's rule can be learned from the משנה; the content continues later.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Not yet stated on this amud; it comes on the next amud.
